page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c3 server family. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for specialized matrix operations.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by moderate single-core capabilities but constrained multi-core and memory performance. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1635.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3703.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 20.97 GB/sec, which falls into the poor tier. Memory performance is also a bottleneck; the Passmark memory score is poor, and uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths are weak at 27.54 GB/sec and 21.03 GB/sec respectively.

The c3-highcpu-4 offers a qualitative cost-efficiency profile suited for workloads that require dedicated compute resources with low memory footprints. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets provides hardware-level acceleration for cryptography and integer operations, as reflected in its average performance in Passmark CPU encryption and single-threaded gzip compression. However, the low memory capacity of 8 GB and weak multi-core scaling present significant tradeoffs for memory-intensive or highly parallelized tasks. This instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, basic text processing, and small-scale computational workloads that do not demand substantial memory bandwidth or large local storage.
